_comment_limits: Deterministic circuit breakers. Seki enforces these. Every value is a hard stop, not a suggestion.

limits._comment_max_concurrent_tickets: How many tickets `orion watch` works at once. Two by default, five is the hard ceiling, and a larger number is clamped rather than honoured. Two is not caution for its own sake: every hazard concurrency introduces -- git against the one shared clone, a budget checkpoint sailed past by runs already in flight, one rate limit reached by several sessions at once, tickets picked that all edit the same files -- is invisible at 1 and obvious at 2. Prove it at 2, then raise it. Note that approvals do not parallelise: N tickets finishing means N approvals waiting on one person.

_comment_gates: Kado, Tate and the plan gate. Turning any of these off removes a control, not a nag.
_comment_paths: Where the artifact chain lives. Relative to repo root.
_comment_autonomy: Per-ENVIRONMENT ceiling. Note the collision: 'dev' here is the dev environment, not the dev branch. propose_only means Orion opens a PR and stops.
_comment_auto_merge: OFF by default and it should stay off until evals/ holds at least min_eval_cases real cases. Green means nothing when the suite is empty.
_comment_budget: YOUR weekly budget, not your Anthropic plan's allowance. Nothing reports how much of a subscription's weekly limit remains, so Orion accounts only for what it spends itself, from the cost and tokens each run returns. Zero means unlimited: a budget nobody set should not be invented. Crossing a checkpoint stops the run until `orion budget ack`.
_comment_slack: A channel per project, and the medium Orion reports into. Needs a Slack APP BOT TOKEN in ORION_SLACK_TOKEN, not an incoming webhook: a webhook is bound to one channel at creation and cannot create any. Scopes: channels:manage (public) or groups:write (private), plus chat:write; after adding a scope you must REINSTALL the app or the existing token will not have it. Channels accumulate like Jira projects and a bot cannot delete them, so archive rather than delete when a project is done. private defaults true because a public channel cannot be made private afterwards, and a slug can reveal an unreleased project.
_comment_vcs: Two long-lived branches. main is the release branch. develop is the integration branch and the default PR base (named develop, not dev, so it does not collide with the dev ENVIRONMENT in the autonomy block). Every task gets its own branch cut from develop. BOTH are push-protected: protecting only main would make the PR into dev optional, and an optional gate is not a gate. work_branch may NOT equal default_branch: Orion merges agent work into work_branch and a HUMAN promotes it to default_branch, so collapsing the two makes every agent merge a release nobody authorised -- Orion refuses that configuration at load, at init and in orion doctor. A repository that genuinely has one branch and no release process sets allow_release_branch_merges: true, which says out loud that the human promotion step is being given up.
_comment_tracker: Leave project_key empty to create a Jira project per idea. That needs the CREATE_PROJECT global permission and accumulates projects a non-admin cannot delete; set project_key to bind an existing project instead. confirm_tree_before_create stays true even under auto_merge: a sandboxed workspace can be deleted, a shared tracker cannot.
_comment_delegation: Handoff to nj-agents. extra_tool_calls_for_review exists because /security-deep-review costs 15-30 agent calls and the breaker counts every one; without a wider envelope a deep review trips the breaker mid-review.
